name: Midwest Ltd
title: Midwest Ltd - 544587 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Quartz volume ramping from ~9,000 t/month, Q2 at 16,000 t, but Q2 quartz EBITDA only break-even-ish and FY27 quartz guidance cut to ~90 crore; operating cash flow negative on receivables and inventory build.

summary.headline: Midwest H1 FY27 revenue grew 24% but quartz segment drag kept EBITDA margin near 12%, with quartz turning EBITDA-positive in Q2.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 revenue up about 24% YoY and Q2 revenue up about 15% YoY, while EBITDA growth lagged at roughly 17% for H1 and about 9% for Q2 as the quartz segment still weighed on margins. Quartz volume ramped to about 16,000 tons in Q2 (monthly run rate ~9,000 tons), and the segment reached a small positive EBITDA in Q2 on a one-off recovery of scrapped material. Operating cash flow was negative, driven by extended domestic credit, higher inventory and settlements, and a fresh JV discounting facility limit issue lifting working capital days to 127 from 104. Management guided to stronger H2 volumes and said quartz should be full-year profitable, but gave no firm numeric EBITDA guidance beyond quartz revenue of about Rs 90 crore for FY27.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 182 crore total company revenue quoted; granite ~Rs 169 crore implied
financial_highlights.change: volume growth ~7% QoQ in Q2; ~14% in H1
Working capital days 127 in H1 FY27 vs 104 in FY26

financial_highlights.value: ~6% of cost base; fuel up 30-35% YoY in H1
financial_highlights.change: fully passed to customers per management

segments.name: Natural stone (granite)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 19% of revenue in H1; H1 standalone EBITDA margin ~18%. Export realisation ~Rs 8,000 per cubic metre for Galaxy and ~Rs 39,000-40,000 for black granite; H1 volume growth ~14%, Q2 ~7%.

segments.name: Quartz
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ~Rs 13 crore vs ~Rs 3 crore in Q1; volume ~16,000 tons in Q2 with a monthly run rate of ~9,000 tons. Realisation ~Rs 8,500/ton; engineered quartz grades range Rs 9,500-14,000/ton. Segment reached small positive EBITDA in Q2, with a targeted full-year profit.

guidance_outlook: Quartz volume targets: Q2 ~15,000 tons (vs earlier 15-20k guidance), Q3 25,000-30,000 tons, Q4 35,000-40,000 tons per the analyst Q&A; company aims for 12,000-15,000 tons monthly next quarter and 15,000-18,000 tons next year.
FY27 quartz revenue estimate ~Rs 90 crore at ~9,000-9,600 realisation; could reach ~Rs 100 crore if 15,000 tons monthly is achieved early.
Quartz expected to be profitable for FY27 on a standalone basis; H2 expected to be much stronger than H1 for granite volumes, with no cyclone disruption expected.
Quartz EBITDA expected to exceed granite EBITDA at full utilisation (12,000-18,000 tons/month), though not yet visible in current cost structure.

Electrification: 10 electric trucks deployed with ~Rs 2-2.5 crore annual savings; plan to convert the full granite fleet (50-60 trucks) within ~24 months; captive/group renewable arrangement saving ~Rs 2/unit with a 1 MW solar plant due this FY.
Medium-term aim (3-4 years): 2.5 per unit growth, EBITDA and 30% ROCE, backed by Rs 300 crore capex plan.
Working capital: management expects days to ease as domestic credit extension is stopped and the JV discounting limit normalises.
capex_capacity: Quartz phase 2 expansion: orders placed; regular (solar/engineered) plant to be commissioned by Q2 FY28 and HPQ plant by about Q3 FY28; ~Rs 120 crore to be spent over the next four quarters.
Quartz phase 1 stabilised at ~9,000-10,000 tons monthly; phase 2 to double processing capacity and add high-purity quartz.
Rs 300 crore capex earmarked for rare earth separation and concentration plants plus phase 2 quartz.
Three new granite mines in Andhra Pradesh awarded via APMDC tender on a fuel-contract basis with minimal upfront investment.

Rare earth projects: Sri Lanka (earliest, permissions expected this quarter, work to start next quarter), Indonesia (definitive agreement targeted this quarter), KMML (stalled pending government team formation).
demand_pricing: Quartz demand from solar glass and engineered stone manufacturers; one large customer could absorb 60,000-70,000 tons/year; supply to Goldstar in Ballari started in Q2.
Quartz realisation ~Rs 8,500/ton on current mix; management said fuel cost increases (~6% impact) were fully passed through with a further ~4% realisation gain and no price rollback planned.
Management is positioning quartz exports to Ireland, Vietnam and Europe but will prioritise domestic demand until volumes exceed 15,000 tons/month.
Rare earth premium pricing expected to persist due to China export restrictions on oxides and growing non-China magnet demand.
Granite export mix: customers typically 60-70% export and 30% domestic; domestic push led to extended credit.

qa_highlights.question: What was quartz volume in Q2 and the run rate, and was it below the earlier 20,000-ton expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 quartz volume was ~16,000 tons, with the latest month at ~9,000 tons; management targets 10,000+ next month and 12,000-15,000 monthly next quarter, with Q3 25,000-30,000 and Q4 35,000-40,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: Why was operating cash flow negative in H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited extended domestic credit (~Rs 25 crore receivables), higher inventory across quartz and granite (~Rs 14 crore), and trade settlements to obtain discounts (~Rs 20 crore), plus a JV discounting limit gap that lifted receivable days; it said no further domestic credit will be extended.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 100-120 crore quartz revenue guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management now expects ~Rs 90 crore for FY27 at current volume and ~9,000-9,600 realisation, and ~Rs 100 crore only if 15,000 tons/month is reached early.

qa_highlights.question: Why did quartz EBITDA margin look higher than the base business in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 benefited from recovering a Q1 contaminated batch that had been scrapped; H1 EBITDA margin is ~12%, and quartz EBITDA is expected to exceed granite once running at 12,000-18,000 tons/month.

qa_highlights.question: What is the granite volume and realisation trend for the remainder of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth ~10-12% plus 3-4% price for ~14-15% revenue growth; realisation ~Rs 8,000/cu m for Galaxy and ~Rs 39,000-40,000 for black granite exports.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the high-wall issue at the mine and when is it resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Rectification is three weeks in; management expects resolution in five to six weeks, with machinery moved to a neighbouring mine so production impact is limited.

risks_watch: Working capital days rose to 127 in H1 FY27 from 104; negative operating cash flow must reverse as receivables from domestic credit and JV discounting normalise.
Quartz still loss-making on a full-year basis; achieving full-year profit depends on the Q3-Q4 volume ramp to 25,000-40,000 tons.
KMML rare earth project stalled pending government team formation; timing not controllable by management.
Fuel price volatility (30-35% YoY increase in H1) and power costs; management says price increases are sticky.
Export tariff risk on quartz to US flagged earlier; management says customers are not affected so far.
Rare earth project execution across Sri Lanka, Indonesia and India is contingent on pending permissions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and cost-saving trajectory and on H2 seasonality, but guarded on timelines for government approvals (KMML, Sri Lanka permissions) and reluctant to give numerical guidance. Notably defensive when explaining negative operating cash flow and the working capital spike.
key_quotes: I am also happy to share that our quartz business has become a bit positive in parallel.
we will be ending up with back profitability for this financial year for the quartz business.
we have not invested much upfront to acquire these mines. It is a tender with raising some fuel contract basis
So we will majorly cater to the customer, our customer will be the one who cater to the domestic market as you mentioned.

adds.what: Quartz phase 2 expansion (regular solar/engineered plant, doubling processing capacity, plus HPQ plant)
Three new granite mines in Andhra Pradesh (APMDC tender, fuel-contract basis)

growth.why: Management guides to stronger H2 volumes and quartz FY27 revenue of about Rs 90 crore (up to Rs 100 crore), backed by phase 1 at ~9,000-10,000 t/month, quartz phase 2 orders placed (~Rs 120 crore over four quarters, regular plant by Q2 FY28, HPQ by Q3 FY28), and a Goldstar supply start, though no firm numeric consolidated EBITDA guidance was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Quartz turned EBITDA-positive in Q2 (partly one-off), H1 consolidated EBITDA margin ~16.37% with quartz dragging, and management expects quartz EBITDA to exceed granite at 12,000-18,000 t/month once volumes ramp; fuel costs (~6% of cost base) passed through with ~4% realisation gain.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Quartz phase 2 orders placed with ~Rs 120 crore over the next four quarters; regular solar/engineered plant by Q2 FY28 and HPQ plant by about Q3 FY28, doubling processing capacity from phase 1 at ~9,000-10,000 t/month.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Quartz guided to 25,000-30,000 t in Q3 and 35,000-40,000 t in Q4 vs ~16,000 t in Q2 with monthly run rate ~9,000 t; granite volume growth ~10-12% in H2 with H1 at ~14%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Rs 300 crore capex earmarked for rare earth separation/concentration plus phase 2 quartz, with Sri Lanka rare earth work expected to start next quarter; utilisation not disclosed but expansion is already committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management cut quartz Q2 volume expectation to ~16,000 t (vs 20,000 earlier expectation), gave FY27 quartz revenue of ~Rs 90 crore (down from Rs 100-120 crore), with ~Rs 100 crore only if 15,000 t/month reached early.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Full-year quartz profitability depends on a steep Q3-Q4 ramp to 25,000-40,000 t, and quartz revenue guidance already fell from Rs 100-120 crore to ~Rs 90 crore; negative operating cash flow and working capital days at 127 (vs 104) add risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: High-purity quartz (HPQ) plant due by about Q3 FY28 and regular solar/engineered quartz plant by Q2 FY28 under phase 2, plus rare earth projects contingent on permissions.

rows.label: Working capital days normalise
rows.why: Working capital days rose to 127 from 104 and operating cash flow was negative; management expects easing once domestic credit extension stops and JV discounting limit normalises, but no numeric target was given.

rows.label: Electrification of granite fleet
rows.why: 10 electric trucks deployed with ~Rs 2-2.5 crore annual savings; plan to convert full fleet of 50-60 trucks within ~24 months, plus 1 MW solar plant due this FY saving ~Rs 2/unit.

rows.label: Quartz large-customer offtake
rows.why: One large customer could absorb 60,000-70,000 t/year and Goldstar supply started in Q2, but volumes depend on ramp to 15,000 t/month before exports are prioritised.
